title: Tables
description: Learn to present tabular data the right way. Master table structure, headers, captions, spanning columns/rows, and how to make tables accessible and keyboard-navigable.
learningObjectives: Structure a data table with thead, tbody, tfoot
Use th with scope for accessible column and row headers
Span cells with colspan and rowspan
Add captions and summaries for accessibility
Know when NOT to use tables (layout vs data)

sections.content: Table Anatomy

An HTML table has a specific structure. <table> is the container. <tr> (table row) creates a row. <td> (table data) creates a data cell. <th> (table header) creates a header cell — bold and centered by default, and critically, it communicates header information to screen readers.

Q1 Sales Data
Product Units Sold Revenue
Pro Plan 1,240 $62,000
Enterprise 85 $127,500
Total 1,325 $189,500
⚠️ Never use tables for page layout. Tables are for tabular data only. Use CSS Flexbox or Grid for layout.
🎯 thead/tbody/tfoot semantically divide the table. Browsers can also use these to keep headers visible when scrolling long tables.

exercises.explanation: caption describes the whole table. thead holds the column headers. tbody holds the data rows.

sections.content: Merging Cells

colspan makes a cell span multiple columns. rowspan makes a cell span multiple rows. The value is the number of columns/rows to span. When you span cells, you must remove the equivalent number of cells from other rows/columns.

Name Score
First Last 95
Weekend Saturday
Sunday

exercises.question: If a cell has colspan="3", how many columns must be removed from adjacent rows to maintain table integrity?
hints: The spanning cell itself counts as 1
exercises.explanation: colspan='3' means this cell occupies 3 column slots. It already counts as 1, so 2 td/th elements must be removed from the same row or adjacent rows where applicable.

sections.content: Making Tables Screen Reader Friendly

Screen readers navigate tables cell-by-cell. Without proper headers, a user hears '$127,500' with zero context. With scope and headers attributes, they hear 'Enterprise plan, Revenue column, $127,500'. The difference is critical for usability.

Monthly Expenses
Category Amount
Rent $1,500
Food $400
💡 scope='col' on column headers and scope='row' on row headers is sufficient for most tables. For complex tables with irregular spans, use the headers attribute with matching IDs.

exercises.question: What does the scope='row' attribute on a <th> cell tell a screen reader?
options: This is a header for the cells in its row
This table has only one row
exercises.correctAnswer: This is a header for the cells in its row
hints: scope describes what the header is *for*
exercises.explanation: scope='row' declares this th as a header for all cells in the same row. The screen reader then announces the row header when reading each data cell in that row.

lessons.title: Table Best Practices & When Not to Use Tables

sections.content: The Golden Rule: Data vs Layout

Tables existed long before CSS. Old websites used tables for entire page layouts — headers, columns, footers. This is now deeply wrong. Tables are exclusively for tabular data: data with meaningful row/column relationships. Use Flexbox and Grid for everything else.
⚠️ Using tables for layout breaks accessibility (screen readers announce row/column info), breaks responsive design, and is flagged by validators.
When Tables ARE Appropriate

Use tables for: pricing comparison charts, data exports, schedules/timetables, sports statistics, financial reports, spreadsheet-like data. All of these have a genuine rows × columns data relationship.

exercises.question: Which of these scenarios is the CORRECT use of an HTML table?
options: A product pricing comparison with rows for features and columns for plans
A navigation menu with two columns
exercises.correctAnswer: A product pricing comparison with rows for features and columns for plans
hints: Tables are for data with row AND column relationships
exercises.explanation: A pricing comparison has a genuine rows-by-columns data relationship (features × plans). The other options are layout — use CSS Grid or Flexbox for those.
